title: The Jews' unbelief and the rejection of the Messiah foretold (Isaiah 53) and Christ's own predictions
source_text: V. Similiter apud Prophetas multis in locis praedicta est incredulitas Judaeorum futura tempore Messiae, & propter eam istius populi futura quoque rejectio. Praesertim apud Isaiam capite quinquagesimo tertio. Quis credidit auditui nostro, & brachium Domini cui est revelatum? Et ibidem haec incredulitas tanta futura esse praedicitur, ut Regem suum Messiam despectui sint habituri, quin & vulneraturi, acerbissimaque & ignominiosissima morte e medio sublaturi, praevaricatoribusque & sceleratis adnumeraturi. Et Messias ipse Jesus Dominus noster, quum in terris versaretur, omnia ista quae primores gentis Judaicae in ipsum admissuri erant, scelera & flagitia sigillatim praedixit, addens oportere ista omnia sic fieri, & sic perficienda omnia quae scripta sunt per Prophetas de filio hominis.
pass_a_gloss: Similarly among the Prophets in many places the unbelief of the Jews to come in the time of the Messiah was foretold, and on account of it the future rejection also of that people. Especially in Isaiah in the fifty-third chapter. Who hath believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed? And in the same place this unbelief is foretold to be going to be so great, that they would hold their King the Messiah in contempt, nay and wound him, and take him away from the midst by a most bitter and most ignominious death, and number him with transgressors and wicked men. And the Messiah himself Jesus our Lord, while he lived on earth, foretold one by one all those crimes and outrages which the chief men of the Jewish nation were going to commit against him, adding that all these things must so come to pass, and that so all things must be accomplished which are written by the Prophets of the son of man.
pass_b_english: In many places the prophets also foretold that the Jews would not believe in the time of the Messiah, and that this people would therefore be rejected. This is especially so in Isaiah 53: 'Who has believed our message, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?'

There the prophet foretells that their unbelief would go so far that they would despise their King, the Messiah, even wound him, remove him by a most cruel and shameful death, and count him among transgressors and criminals. And the Messiah himself, Jesus our Lord, while he lived on earth, foretold one by one all the crimes and outrages that the leaders of the Jewish nation would commit against him. He added that all this must happen so, and that everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man must be fulfilled in this way.

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
